status.note: Built against ADR 0006. No panel was drawn in the design source — the mock shows only the tab row — so its padding is the one value here with no measured original behind it.

intent.purpose: The content one tab reveals. It exists so the tab list has something real to control: a tab that announces it opens a panel, with no panel wired to it, describes an interaction that does not happen.
behaviour: Matches its `value` against the selection on the surrounding Tabs and hides itself when it does not match. Visibility is the `hidden` attribute, not a styled state — the panel is either present or removed from the page outright, never faded, so there is no `states` block here to declare.
Stays mounted while hidden, using the `hidden` attribute. Scroll position, form state and anything a consumer measured survive switching away and back.
Is focusable in its own right, so a keyboard user moving on from the tab has somewhere to land even when the panel holds nothing focusable.
Names itself from its tab, via aria-labelledby, so the panel is announced with the tab's label rather than needing its own.
Throws if rendered outside a Tabs.
notFor: Content that should unmount when hidden. This panel stays in the DOM by design; anything expensive enough to need unmounting should be guarded by the consumer inside the panel.
Lazy loading. Nothing here defers rendering, and activation follows focus on the parent, so arrowing across the tabs renders every panel in turn.
Use outside a Tabs, or without a TabItem of the same value — the panel would have no accessible name and no way to be shown.

a11y.keyboard: Reachable with Tab immediately after the selected tab. It shows no focus ring of its own.
notes: `tabIndex={0}` is unconditional, which is the WAI-ARIA practice for a panel that may hold no focusable content. The cost is a Tab stop on every panel, including ones that are full of focusable content and did not need it.

The panel takes no focus ring, so a keyboard user landing on it gets no visible confirmation. That is the common convention for tab panels and it is still a real gap for anyone who cannot infer position from the scroll.

The accessible name comes entirely from the matching TabItem. If no item carries the same `value`, aria-labelledby points at a missing id and the panel is announced unnamed. Nothing detects that pairing.
Contrast is not applicable: the panel paints no colour of its own and inherits whatever it is placed on.

children.description: Anything. The panel makes no assumptions about its content and applies no layout beyond the space above it.

root.description: The panel region. Its only paint is the space separating it from the tab row.
